capsuleTopic.title: Kingdom
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Realm · rule · promise · proclamation · inheritance · reign
capsuleTopic.orientation: Trace every explicit Kingdom occurrence through a curated whole-canon trail across human realms, Israel’s monarchy, prayer and prophecy, later Jewish memory, Jesus’ proclamation, mission, communities, and Revelation—without treating every use as one undifferentiated idea.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Enter the trail and inspect who names the Kingdom, which realm is in view, what action occurs, and how each context changes the word’s force.

passages.observation: Obadiah ends with deliverers on Zion, judgment on Esau’s mountain, and the LORD’s kingdom.

passages.title: Former dominion returns to Jerusalem
passages.excerpt: You, tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come. Yes, the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
passages.observation: A restored kingdom is announced after nations stream to Zion and swords become farming tools.

passages.title: The thrones of kingdoms overthrown
passages.excerpt: I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overthrow the chariots and those who ride in them. The hors…
passages.observation: The oracle names shaking, overturned thrones, broken military strength, and Zerubbabel as a signet.

passages.title: Tobit blesses the everlasting King
passages.excerpt: And Tobit wrote a prayer for rejoicing, and said, “Blessed is God who lives forever! Blessed is his kingdom!
passages.observation: Tobit’s prayer blesses God and God’s kingdom while holding chastening, mercy, scattering, and gathering together.

passages.title: Wisdom’s path reaches a kingdom
passages.excerpt: So then desire for wisdom promotes to a kingdom.
passages.observation: The sequence moves from desire for instruction through love, law, incorruption, nearness to God, and kingdom.

passages.title: Samuel establishes a kingdom
passages.excerpt: Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, loved by his Lord, established a kingdom and anointed princes over his people.
passages.observation: The remembered Samuel is prophet, judge, intercessor, and anointer of rulers.

passages.title: David inherits an enduring throne
passages.excerpt: David inherited the throne of a kingdom forever and ever for being merciful.
passages.observation: Mattathias’s final exhortation remembers David’s mercy and the throne of a kingdom.

passages.title: Heritage, kingdom, priesthood, and consecration restored
passages.excerpt: Now God, who saved all his people, and restored the heritage to all, with the kingdom, the priesthood, and the consecration,
passages.observation: The letter’s prayer gathers rescue, heritage, kingdom, priesthood, holiness, and mercy.

passages.title: Truth named as kingdom and power
passages.excerpt: In truth’s judgment is not any unrighteousness. Truth is the strength, the kingdom, the power, and the majesty of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth!”
passages.observation: The contest speech places strength, kingdom, power, and majesty under the judgment of truth.

passages.title: A kingdom already prepared
passages.excerpt: Ask, and you will receive. Pray that your days may be few, that they may be shortened. The kingdom is already prepared for you. Watch!
passages.observation: The address joins asking, shortened days, watchfulness, prepared kingdom, and promised light.

passages.title: The Kingdom of Heaven draws near
passages.excerpt: “Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!”
passages.observation: John’s wilderness proclamation joins repentance with the nearness of the Kingdom of Heaven.

passages.title: The Kingdom belongs to the poor in spirit
passages.excerpt: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
passages.observation: The opening beatitude places present possession of the Kingdom beside poverty of spirit.

passages.title: A prayer for the Kingdom to come
passages.excerpt: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
passages.observation: The prayer places God’s name, Kingdom, will, daily bread, forgiveness, and deliverance in sequence.

passages.title: The Kingdom comes in an exorcism dispute
passages.excerpt: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
passages.observation: Jesus contrasts a divided satanic kingdom with casting out demons by God’s Spirit.

passages.title: Kingdom mysteries given and withheld
passages.excerpt: He answered them, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but it is not given to them.
passages.observation: Jesus distinguishes what is given to the disciples from what is received by those who hear in parables.

passages.title: A child placed among the disciples
passages.excerpt: In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?”
passages.observation: A question about greatness leads Jesus to place a child in their midst and speak about turning, entering, and humility.

passages.title: Wealth and entering the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.
passages.observation: The rich man’s departure leads to statements about difficulty, impossibility, God’s action, and what disciples have left.

passages.title: The Kingdom and its fruit
passages.excerpt: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.
passages.observation: After a vineyard parable, Jesus speaks of the Kingdom being taken and given to a people producing its fruit.

passages.title: Inherit the prepared Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
passages.observation: The Son of Man’s judgment scene joins throne, nations, separation, inheritance, and acts toward vulnerable people.

passages.title: The time is fulfilled
passages.excerpt: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,
passages.observation: After John’s arrest, Jesus announces God’s Good News, fulfilled time, a near Kingdom, repentance, and belief.

passages.title: Seed grows while the sower sleeps
passages.excerpt: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
passages.observation: The Kingdom is compared to seed whose growth occurs through night, day, stages, and harvest.

passages.title: Receive the Kingdom like a child
passages.excerpt: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such a…
passages.observation: Jesus responds to hindered children with belonging, receiving, entering, touch, and blessing.

passages.title: Joseph waits for God’s Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
passages.observation: Joseph’s expectation is named as he boldly asks Pilate for Jesus’ body and arranges burial.

passages.title: A Kingdom with no end
passages.excerpt: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.”
passages.observation: Gabriel joins David’s throne, Jacob’s house, everlasting reign, and an unending Kingdom in the announcement to Mary.

passages.title: Sent to announce God’s Kingdom
passages.excerpt: But he said to them, “I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”
passages.observation: Jesus explains his movement to other cities by saying that he must proclaim God’s Kingdom.

passages.title: May your Kingdom come
passages.excerpt: He said to them, “When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
passages.observation: Luke’s prayer places holy name, coming Kingdom, bread, forgiveness, and testing together.

passages.title: The Father gives the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
passages.observation: The little flock is told not to fear because the Father delights to give the Kingdom, followed by instructions about possessions and treasure.

passages.title: Asked when the Kingdom would come
passages.excerpt: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
passages.observation: Jesus answers a timing question by denying observable location claims and naming the Kingdom’s presence among them.

passages.title: A kingdom expected immediately
passages.excerpt: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.
passages.observation: Because Jerusalem is near and the crowd expects immediate revelation, Jesus tells of a nobleman receiving a kingdom and returning.

passages.title: A Kingdom conferred at the table
passages.excerpt: I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
passages.observation: At the final meal, Jesus speaks of testing, service, a conferred kingdom, table fellowship, thrones, and judgment.

passages.title: Seeing and entering God’s Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Jesus answered him, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”
passages.observation: Jesus answers Nicodemus with birth anew, water, Spirit, flesh, wind, and entry into God’s Kingdom.

passages.title: A Kingdom not from here
passages.excerpt: Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my…
passages.observation: Before Pilate, Jesus distinguishes his Kingdom’s source from worldly rule and points to servants who do not fight to prevent his arrest.

passages.title: Forty days of Kingdom speech
passages.excerpt: To these he also showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days and speaking about God’s Kingdom.
passages.observation: Acts opens with appearances, proofs, Kingdom teaching, Spirit promise, a restoration question, and an expanding witness commission.

passages.title: Kingdom proclamation in Samaria
passages.excerpt: But when they believed Philip preaching good news about God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
passages.observation: Philip’s Good News about God’s Kingdom and Jesus’ name is followed by belief and baptism.

passages.title: Affliction and entering the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.
passages.observation: Paul and Barnabas strengthen disciples, urge continuance, speak of affliction, and appoint elders on their return journey.

passages.title: Kingdom witness in Rome
passages.excerpt: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them about Jesus,…
passages.observation: Paul explains God’s Kingdom and persuades about Jesus from Moses and the prophets before the book ends with unhindered teaching.

passages.title: Not eating and drinking
passages.excerpt: for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
passages.observation: Paul contrasts food disputes with righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit as the character of God’s Kingdom.

passages.title: Not in word but in power
passages.excerpt: For God’s Kingdom is not in word, but in power.
passages.observation: Paul contrasts speech and power while addressing boasting, apostolic presence, discipline, love, and gentleness.

passages.title: The Kingdom delivered to the Father
passages.excerpt: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God the Father, when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.
passages.observation: The resurrection argument moves through order, coming, Kingdom, abolished powers, reign, enemies, and death.

passages.title: Transferred into the Son’s Kingdom
passages.excerpt: who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love,
passages.observation: The thanksgiving joins rescue from darkness, transfer, redemption, creation, firstborn language, and reconciliation.

passages.title: The royal psalm is spoken of the Son
passages.excerpt: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.
passages.observation: Hebrews quotes the everlasting throne and equitable scepter while contrasting the Son with angels.

passages.title: Receiving an unshakable Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Therefore, receiving a Kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s have grace, through which we serve God acceptably, with reverence and awe,
passages.observation: The passage contrasts Sinai and Zion, warning and promise, shaken creation and what remains.

passages.title: The poor named as Kingdom heirs
passages.excerpt: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?
passages.observation: James contrasts God’s choice of the poor with the assembly’s preference for the richly dressed.

passages.title: Made a Kingdom and priests
passages.phase: The world’s kingdom and enduring reign
passages.excerpt: and he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father—to him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
passages.observation: The opening blessing moves through witness, firstborn, rule, love, blood, release, Kingdom, priests, and coming.

passages.title: The world’s kingdom becomes God’s and Christ’s
passages.phase: The world’s kingdom and enduring reign
passages.excerpt: The seventh angel sounded, and great voices in heaven followed, saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ. He will reign f…
passages.observation: The seventh trumpet brings heavenly voices, worship, wrath, judgment, reward, and an everlasting reign.

passages.title: Kingdom announced after the accuser falls
passages.phase: The world’s kingdom and enduring reign
passages.excerpt: I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come; for the accuser of our bro…
passages.observation: A loud heavenly voice joins salvation, power, Kingdom, Christ’s authority, accusation, blood, testimony, and endurance.

passages.title: Hazor heads the northern kingdoms
passages.excerpt: Joshua turned back at that time, and took Hazor, and struck its king with the sword; for Hazor used to be the head of all those kingdoms.
passages.observation: Joshua takes Hazor after the northern coalition gathers, and the narrator identifies the city as the former head of those kingdoms.

passages.title: Cyrus proclaims throughout his kingdom
passages.excerpt: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the LORD’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia,…
passages.observation: The LORD stirs Cyrus to issue a written proclamation that credits the God of heaven with the kingdoms of the earth and authorizes a house in Jerusalem.

passages.title: From prison into a kingdom
passages.excerpt: For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
passages.observation: The reflection places a poor youth who becomes king beside an old ruler who no longer receives admonition.

passages.title: The northern kingdom will cease
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to him, “Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and will cause the kingdom of the ho…
passages.observation: The naming of Jezreel joins remembered bloodshed with an announced end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.

passages.title: A kingdom exposed before kingdoms
passages.excerpt: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
passages.observation: Nineveh’s violence and sorceries lead into an oracle of exposure before nations and kingdoms.

passages.title: Kingdoms assembled for judgment
passages.excerpt: “Therefore wait for me”, says the LORD, “until the day that I rise up to the prey, for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms to p…
passages.observation: The LORD’s call to wait names gathered nations, assembled kingdoms, indignation, fire, and a later change of speech.

passages.title: Nebuchadnezzar swears by throne and kingdom
passages.excerpt: And Nebuchadnezzar was exceedingly angry with all this land, and he swore by his throne and kingdom that he would surely be avenged upon all the coasts of Cilicia, Dam…
passages.observation: The ruler’s anger becomes an oath of vengeance after western peoples refuse his summons to war.

passages.title: A dispersed people accused within the empire
passages.excerpt: So he spoke to King Ahasuerus, saying, “There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws differ from all the other nations. They disob…
passages.observation: Haman describes a people scattered through the kingdom and uses their distinct laws to support a proposal for destruction.

passages.title: Scattered under surrounding kingdoms
passages.excerpt: Moreover he has given them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the people around us, where the Lord…
passages.observation: The confession names subjection, reproach, desolation, scattering, and refusal to hear the Lord’s voice.

passages.title: Cruelty called harmful to the kingdom
passages.excerpt: “You have governed badly, and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty. You have labored to deprive me, your benefactor, at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devisi…
passages.observation: The prayer addresses a ruler whose secret measures against his benefactor are described as tyranny and injury to the kingdom.

passages.title: A kingdom received and abused
passages.excerpt: “Impious tyrant, and most blasphemous man, were you not ashamed, having received prosperity and a kingdom from God, to kill His servants, and to rack the doers of godl…
passages.observation: The martyr addresses Antiochus as one who received prosperity and a kingdom from God yet kills and tortures God’s servants.

passages.title: The saints receive the kingdom
passages.excerpt: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’
passages.observation: The vision’s interpretation places beastly kingdoms beside the saints receiving and possessing the kingdom forever.

passages.title: The kingdoms of the world are offered
passages.excerpt: Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
passages.observation: The tempter displays the world’s kingdoms and their glory, attaching their transfer to an act of worship.

passages.title: Teaching, proclaiming, and healing through Galilee
passages.excerpt: Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
passages.observation: Matthew summarizes Jesus moving through Galilee with synagogue teaching, Kingdom proclamation, and healing.

passages.title: Righteousness and entering the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
passages.observation: Jesus places entry into the Kingdom beside a righteousness that exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees.

passages.title: Saying Lord and doing the Father’s will
passages.excerpt: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
passages.observation: Jesus distinguishes verbal address from doing the will of his Father in the warning about entering the Kingdom.

passages.title: The Twelve announce a near Kingdom
passages.excerpt: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’
passages.observation: Jesus sends the Twelve with a near-Kingdom announcement accompanied by healing, restoration, and freely given action.

passages.title: John and the least in the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven i…
passages.observation: Jesus speaks of John’s greatness and then distinguishes the least in the Kingdom of Heaven.

passages.title: Kingdom images accumulate in parables
passages.excerpt: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,
passages.observation: Seed, weeds, mustard, yeast, treasure, pearl, net, and a householder remain distinct images inside one sustained discourse.

passages.title: Keys, binding, and releasing
passages.excerpt: I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been r…
passages.observation: Jesus’ response to Peter joins assembly, gates, Kingdom keys, binding, and releasing.

passages.title: Kingdom news as testimony to all nations
passages.excerpt: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
passages.observation: The discourse places worldwide Kingdom proclamation amid deception, conflict, endurance, testimony, and the end.

passages.title: Ten virgins wait for the bridegroom
passages.excerpt: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
passages.observation: The parable distinguishes preparation and delay through lamps, oil, sleep, a midnight cry, entry, and a shut door.

passages.title: The Kingdom seen coming with power
passages.excerpt: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
passages.observation: Jesus places a saying about some standing there seeing God’s Kingdom beside the transfiguration that follows.

passages.title: Authority over the world’s kingdoms is offered
passages.excerpt: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
passages.observation: The devil displays the world’s kingdoms, claims authority over them, and asks Jesus for worship.

passages.title: Kingdom news travels with a named company
passages.excerpt: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
passages.observation: Jesus moves through cities and villages proclaiming God’s Kingdom with the Twelve and named women who support the group.

passages.title: Sent to proclaim and heal
passages.excerpt: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
passages.observation: Jesus gives the Twelve power and authority, then sends them to proclaim God’s Kingdom and heal the sick.

passages.title: The Kingdom comes near in receiving or rejecting towns
passages.excerpt: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
passages.observation: The sent disciples heal and announce nearness in receptive towns, while rejected towns receive the same nearness statement with a public sign.

passages.title: Mustard and yeast placed side by side
passages.excerpt: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
passages.observation: Jesus asks what God’s Kingdom resembles and answers with two images of small beginnings and spreading effects.

passages.title: Law, prophets, John, and Kingdom news
passages.excerpt: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
passages.observation: Jesus marks a sequence from law and prophets to John and then to the proclamation of God’s Kingdom.

passages.title: The meal awaits fulfillment in the Kingdom
passages.excerpt: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
passages.observation: At the table Jesus joins Passover, suffering, future fulfillment, cup, Kingdom, bread, and remembrance.

passages.title: Remember me in your Kingdom
passages.excerpt: He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
passages.observation: One condemned man rebukes the other, acknowledges judgment, addresses Jesus, and asks to be remembered in his Kingdom.

passages.title: Reasoning for three months in Ephesus
passages.excerpt: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things about God’s Kingdom.
passages.observation: Paul speaks boldly in the synagogue, reasoning and persuading about God’s Kingdom until public resistance redirects the setting.

passages.title: Kingdom proclamation recalled among elders
passages.excerpt: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
passages.observation: Paul’s farewell recalls his movement among the Ephesian elders and places Kingdom proclamation within his accounting of ministry.

passages.title: Acts ends with unhindered Kingdom teaching
passages.excerpt: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
passages.observation: Paul remains in rented lodging, welcomes visitors, proclaims God’s Kingdom, and teaches about Jesus with boldness and no hindrance.

passages.title: Inheritance warning amid community disputes
passages.excerpt: Or don’t you know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s Kingdom? Don’t be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostit…
passages.observation: Paul’s warning about inheriting God’s Kingdom follows a dispute over lawsuits and names practices that contradict the community’s washed identity.

passages.title: Perishable flesh and Kingdom inheritance
passages.excerpt: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
passages.observation: The resurrection argument contrasts flesh and blood with inheritance and the perishable with imperishability before announcing transformation.

passages.title: Works, fruit, and Kingdom inheritance
passages.excerpt: envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these; of which I forewarn you, even as I also forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit…
passages.observation: The warning about practices that do not inherit God’s Kingdom stands between the works of the flesh and the fruit of the Spirit.

passages.title: Inheritance in the Kingdom of Christ and God
passages.excerpt: Know this for sure, that no sexually immoral person, nor unclean person, nor covetous man (who is an idolater), has any inheritance in the Kingdom of Christ and God.
passages.observation: The letter links a Kingdom inheritance warning with sexual immorality, impurity, covetousness, thanksgiving, and walking as children of light.

passages.title: Called into God’s Kingdom and glory
passages.excerpt: to the end that you should walk worthily of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.
passages.observation: Paul recalls exhorting each person toward a walk worthy of the God who calls them into his Kingdom and glory.

passages.title: Suffering and God’s Kingdom
passages.excerpt: This is an obvious sign of the righteous judgment of God, to the end that you may be counted worthy of God’s Kingdom, for which you also suffer.
passages.observation: The letter reads endurance in persecutions as evidence within God’s righteous judgment and names the Kingdom for which the community suffers.

passages.title: Appearing, judgment, and Kingdom
passages.excerpt: I command you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and his Kingdom:
passages.observation: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ Jesus, joining judgment of living and dead with appearing and Kingdom.

passages.title: Entrance richly supplied
passages.excerpt: For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.
passages.observation: The letter joins calling, election, practiced qualities, stability, and entrance into the eternal Kingdom of Jesus Christ.

passages.title: The beast’s kingdom is darkened
passages.phase: The world’s kingdom and enduring reign
passages.excerpt: The fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and his kingdom was darkened. They gnawed their tongues because of the pain,
passages.observation: The fifth bowl falls on the beast’s throne, darkening his kingdom while pain and blasphemy continue without repentance.

passages.title: Ten kings receive brief authority
passages.phase: The world’s kingdom and enduring reign
passages.excerpt: The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority as kings with the beast for one hour.
passages.observation: The angel interprets ten horns as kings who receive authority with the beast for one hour and give their power to him.
